title: Test and Monitor with CloudWatch
content:
Test and Monitor with CloudWatch In this section, we will invoke the AWS Lambda CSV Processor, verify the JSON result in Amazon S3, and use Amazon CloudWatch to inspect execution logs.
Amazon CloudWatch is an AWS monitoring and observability service that collects Metrics, Logs, and resource operation information.
For this exercise, CloudWatch Logs help determine whether Lambda processing succeeded or encountered an execution error.
1. Prepare the testing environment Complete:
Section 5.10.1 - Set Up Amazon S3 and Prepare Data. Section 5.10.2 - Configure IAM Execution Role. Section 5.10.3 - Build the AWS Lambda CSV Processor. Verify the resources:
Region: ap-southeast-1 Bucket: sap-data-project-2026-huflit01 Lambda: sap-csv-processor-demo Input: lambda-demo/input/registrations.csv Output: lambda-demo/processed/registrations-result.json 2. Invoke Lambda using a Test Event Open the AWS Lambda Console. Select sap-csv-processor-demo. Select Test. Select the SAPCSVProcessingTest Event. Choose Test to invoke the Function. Lambda retrieves the input CSV, processes the records, and writes a JSON result to Amazon S3.
3. Inspect the Execution Result Review the Execution result after invocation.
Expected response:
{ "statusCode": 200, "body": "{\"total\": 4, \"valid\": 2, \"duplicates\": 1, \"invalid\": 1}" } Explanation:
total: Number of processed records. valid: Number of valid unique records. duplicates: Number of duplicate student IDs. invalid: Number of records missing required information. Actual results from the November 9, 2026 project exercise:
Total records: 4 Valid records: 2 Duplicate records: 1 Invalid records: 1 Lambda returned statusCode 200.
This is the Function’s Test Event response rather than an HTTP response from API Gateway or a Lambda Function URL.
4. Compare results with the input CSV Workshop input:
mssv,full_name DEMO001,Student A DEMO002,Student B DEMO001,Student A ,Student C Expected classifications:
Record Classification DEMO001 - Student A Valid DEMO002 - Student B Valid DEMO001 - Student A Duplicate Missing Student ID - Student C Invalid Verify:
Total = Valid + Duplicates + Invalid = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 The summary should accurately reflect the input records.
5. Verify the JSON result in Amazon S3 Open Amazon S3 Console. Select sap-data-project-2026-huflit01. Open lambda-demo/processed/. Locate: registrations-result.json Download the Object and inspect its content.
Expected JSON:
{ "total": 4, "valid": 2, "duplicates": 1, "invalid": 1 } Inspect Last modified to confirm that the Object was created or updated during the current test.
If an output Object already exists, its presence alone does not demonstrate that the latest invocation succeeded.
6. Verify using AWS CLI Use PowerShell to inspect the JSON result:
aws s3 cp s3://sap-data-project-2026-huflit01/lambda-demo/processed/registrations-result.json - --region ap-southeast-1 --profile sap-dev Expected output:
{"total": 4, "valid": 2, "duplicates": 1, "invalid": 1} Inspect Object metadata:
aws s3api head-object ` --bucket sap-data-project-2026-huflit01 ` --key lambda-demo/processed/registrations-result.json ` --region ap-southeast-1 ` --profile sap-dev The AWS CLI Profile requires appropriate read permissions for the output Object.
7. Open CloudWatch Logs In the Lambda Console:
Select sap-csv-processor-demo. Select Monitor. Choose View CloudWatch logs if available. Alternatively, open:
Amazon CloudWatch Console
In CloudWatch:
Select ap-southeast-1. Select Logs. Select Log groups. Locate: /aws/lambda/sap-csv-processor-demo The Log Group is typically created when Lambda executes with appropriate CloudWatch Logs permissions.
8. Inspect the Log Stream Open the Function’s Log Group. Select the Log Stream associated with the latest invocation. Inspect its Log Events. Typical execution log information:
START RequestId: ... SAP S3 demo processed: {"total": 4, "valid": 2, "duplicates": 1, "invalid": 1} END RequestId: ... REPORT RequestId: ... Explanation:
START: Beginning of an invocation. RequestId: Invocation identifier. Application Log: Processing information recorded by the Function. END: End of execution. REPORT: Execution duration and memory information. 9. Analyze actual execution results During the November 9, 2026 test, CloudWatch recorded:
Metric Result Execution Duration 404.97 ms Billed Duration 892 ms Memory Size 128 MB Max Memory Used 93 MB The historical output Object size was 55 B.
Duration The Function execution time recorded in the REPORT Log:
404.97 ms Billed Duration The execution time used for Lambda billing calculations:
892 ms Billed Duration may include billable initialization time depending on the execution environment.
Memory Size Configured Function memory:
128 MB Max Memory Used Maximum recorded memory usage:
93 MB The configured 128 MB memory was sufficient for the small historical test dataset.
These are historical project results. Execution duration, memory usage, and JSON Object size may differ when using the reconstructed workshop code, another Runtime, or different data. One successful invocation does not establish large-scale Production processing capacity.
10. Configure CloudWatch Log Retention To manage log storage:
Open CloudWatch Console. Select Logs → Log groups. Select /aws/lambda/sap-csv-processor-demo. Choose Actions or Edit retention setting. Set retention to: 7 days Save the configuration. The project configured a seven-day retention period for its Lambda logs.
This helps limit unnecessary long-term log storage.
Expired log deletion follows CloudWatch’s retention mechanism and may not occur immediately.
11. Test error scenarios Scenario 1: Missing input Object In a dedicated test Function, temporarily configure INPUT_KEY to reference an Object that does not exist.
To specifically test NoSuchKey, the Function must be authorized to read that Key. Otherwise, S3 may return AccessDenied.
Invoke the Function and verify:
Lambda reports an execution error. No successful result is returned. CloudWatch records error information. Restore the original INPUT_KEY after testing.
Scenario 2: Missing CSV columns Prepare a test CSV without mssv or full_name.
The Function should identify the invalid file structure and report an error.
Use a separate test Object and appropriate IAM permissions rather than overwriting active source data.
Scenario 3: Empty CSV dataset A file containing only valid column headers should produce:
{ "total": 0, "valid": 0, "duplicates": 0, "invalid": 0 } Scenario 4: Insufficient S3 permissions Inspect AccessDenied when the Function does not have the required Object permissions.
Do not remove permissions from shared Roles used by other applications solely to create a test failure.
These error scenarios are additional workshop tests. Do not report them as PASS until they have been performed and verified.
12. Explore future S3 Event Notification integration The current exercise invokes Lambda using a Test Event.
An event-driven extension could automatically process new CSV uploads:
Upload CSV | v Amazon S3 - Input Prefix | | ObjectCreated Event v AWS Lambda | v Amazon S3 - Processed Prefix This architecture would require:
S3 Event Notification configuration. Permission for S3 to invoke Lambda. S3 Event processing in the Lambda Handler. Input Prefix filtering. Duplicate event handling and appropriate output generation. Only Objects under the input Prefix should trigger processing.
Do not configure a broad Trigger for the entire Bucket when Lambda writes results back to that Bucket, because this may cause recursive invocations.
This is a future extension rather than verified functionality in the current Demo.
13. Summarize the results Results recorded during the November 9, 2026 exercise:
Test Result S3 Input CSV PASS Lambda Execution Role PASS Lambda Test Event PASS CSV Processing PASS Total Records 4 Valid Records 2 Duplicate Records 1 Invalid Records 1 Lambda statusCode 200 S3 Output JSON PASS CloudWatch Logs PASS Log Retention 7 days 14. Evaluate the Serverless architecture Advantages:
No dedicated CSV processing server to manage. Separate input and output data in S3. Controlled resource access through IAM. Execution observability using CloudWatch. Suitable for independent data processing tasks. Current Demo limitations:
Lambda is manually invoked using Test Events. Output contains summary counts rather than a cleaned registration dataset. Registration records are not automatically written to DynamoDB. The CSV file is read entirely into memory. Large-file processing performance has not been validated. The output uses a fixed Object Key. Future improvements:
Automated S3 event-driven processing. Unique output Keys for individual input files. Idempotency mechanisms. More comprehensive business validation. Appropriate large-file processing architecture. Integration with the application Import workflow where required. Conclusion In this section, we implemented an AWS Serverless Data Processing workflow using Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, IAM, and CloudWatch.
Lambda read CSV data, classified valid, duplicate, and invalid records, and stored a JSON result in Amazon S3.
CloudWatch Logs provided execution information, processing duration, and memory usage evidence.
This exercise extends the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform with an independent Serverless data processing component.
Next: Clean Up AWS Resources

title: Test the Interface and System Functionality
content:
Test the Interface and System Functionality In this section, we will test the React/Vite interface and its communication with the FastAPI Backend of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
The objective is to verify that users can perform business operations through the Web interface and inspect consistency between the Frontend, Backend, and stored data.
1. Prepare the testing environment Ensure that the following components are available:
FastAPI Backend on port 8000. React/Vite Frontend running locally. SQLite Local Persistence. Amazon DynamoDB Integration when testing AWS Pilot functionality. ADMIN and STUDENT Demo accounts. Use synthetic student data to avoid affecting real student information.
Open the application:
http://localhost:5173
2. Test the login interface On the login page, perform the following tests:
Sign in using valid ADMIN credentials. Sign in using valid STUDENT credentials. Enter an incorrect password. Leave required fields empty. Expected results:
Valid users can access the system. Invalid input is handled with an appropriate message. The interface displayed after login matches the user’s Role. 3. Test the ADMIN Home page Sign in using an ADMIN account.
Review the system’s Home page and Sidebar.
Verify the following functionality groups:
Activity Management. Student Account Management. Registration and Attendance Management. Evidence Management. Reconciliation and Participation Confirmation. Analytics Dashboard. Personal Profile. Navigate between pages to verify interface stability and appropriate data loading.
4. Test Activity Management Step 1: Open the activity list From the ADMIN interface, open Activity Management.
Verify the activity list retrieved from the Backend.
Step 2: Create a Demo activity Select the function for creating a new activity.
Enter sample information:
Activity Name: AWS Workshop Demo Location: University Hall Description: Student Activity Management Platform Testing Enter the scheduled time and required fields according to the current application form.
Save the activity.
Step 3: Verify the result After successful creation:
The activity appears in the activity list. Activity information is displayed correctly. The activity details page is accessible. An Activity ID is available for subsequent tests. If the activity is created in DRAFT status, apply the appropriate state transition before testing registration or attendance operations.
Step 4: Verify Backend data Open Developer Tools and inspect the activity creation API request.
If the Activities AWS Pilot is enabled, verify the item in SAP-Activities according to section 5.4.
If using Local Demo mode, inspect the data through the current persistence mechanism.
5. Test Student Account Management From the ADMIN interface, open Student Account Management.
Verify:
The student account list. Search or filtering if supported by the interface. Account status information. Account locking and unlocking. Password reset functionality. Student account synchronization. Test account locking and unlocking Use a dedicated synthetic student account:
Select the test account. Lock the account. Verify the updated account status. Attempt to sign in using the locked account in a separate browser window. Verify that the Backend denies login or access according to the account rules. Return to the ADMIN interface and unlock the account. Verify that the account can sign in again. Test password reset Use a dedicated Demo account.
Select the password reset function. Enter a temporary password that satisfies Backend requirements. Confirm the operation. Verify login using the new password. Do not capture or disclose temporary passwords in the internship report.
Only test account status changes and password resets using Demo accounts. Do not use real student accounts or synchronize real student data without authorization.
6. Test business operation interfaces Verify that the business operation pages are accessible through the Frontend.
Registration Import Open the registration import interface. Inspect the CSV/XLSX file selection area. Verify the selected activity information. Ensure that the interface accepts appropriate files. Attendance Management Open the Check-in/Check-out interface. Verify manual student ID input or input from a compatible scanner. Inspect student and activity information. Review the attendance result display. Attendance is recorded in real time through REST APIs. Importing attendance spreadsheets after an activity is not the primary recording mechanism.
Evidence Import Open the participation evidence import interface. Inspect the CSV/XLSX upload area. Verify activity information and data processing controls. Reconciliation and Participation Open the data reconciliation interface. Review student records and data status information. Inspect participation confirmation controls available to ADMIN users. Detailed exercises covering Registration, Attendance, Evidence, and Participation will be presented in sections 5.6 and 5.7.
7. Test the Analytics Dashboard Open the Analytics Dashboard using an ADMIN account.
Review indicators available in the current system:
Total Activities. Total Registrations. Attendance information. Participation results. Activity-based statistics. Change available filters if supported by the interface.
Verify that displayed data updates according to the selected activity or filter.
The Dashboard is developed using React/Vite and consumes data provided by FastAPI.
Amazon QuickSight is not used as the Dashboard implementation in the current project.
8. Test the STUDENT interface Sign out of the ADMIN account and sign in using a STUDENT Demo account.
Verify:
Student Home page. Authorized activity information. Personal participation results. Personal profile. Logout functionality. In particular, confirm that Student Account Management does not appear in the STUDENT interface.
Attempt to access a known administrative route from the ADMIN interface.
Expected results:
The Frontend restricts unauthorized access or redirects to an appropriate page. The Backend rejects administrative API requests using a STUDENT Access Token. 9. Test session behavior after reloading Sign in using a Demo account.
Perform the following steps:
Open Activity Management or the personal profile page. Press F5 to reload the page. Verify the login session. Verify current user information. Verify data retrieval from the Backend. Expected results:
A valid authentication session is restored according to the existing implementation. The interface reflects the appropriate Role. Data is retrieved again. No JavaScript errors occur due to uninitialized authentication state. 10. Test responsive interface behavior Open Developer Tools.
Select Toggle Device Toolbar to simulate different screen sizes.
Test the application on:
Desktop screen sizes. Tablet screen sizes. Mobile screen sizes. Inspect:
Login page. Sidebar and navigation. Activity creation forms. Student data tables. Analytics Dashboard. Record any layout limitations for future interface improvements.
11. Inspect Frontend errors Use Developer Tools:
Console: Inspect JavaScript errors. Network: Inspect failed HTTP requests. Application: Inspect authentication session state. Elements: Inspect interface layout. If the Frontend does not display data, verify:
Backend availability. API_BASE_URL configuration. Access Token validity. Compatibility between API Responses and the Frontend data model. User Role and permissions. During development, prioritize actual API-based data and authentication instead of obsolete Mock Authentication mechanisms.
12. Summarize interface test results Test Case Expected Result Login Successful login with valid credentials ADMIN Dashboard Administrative functionality displayed Create Activity Activity created and displayed Student Accounts ADMIN can manage student accounts Lock/Unlock Account status updated Reset Password New password is usable Registration Interface Activity and file selection available Attendance Interface Attendance operations available Evidence Interface Evidence file imports available Reconciliation Reconciliation data displayed Analytics Dashboard Statistical information displayed STUDENT Dashboard Only authorized functionality displayed Page Reload Valid authentication session restored Logout Authentication state cleared Responsive Layout Interface usable at tested screen sizes This table defines testing criteria. Workshop participants should record actual results and capture corresponding evidence.
13. Prepare the Frontend for the next stage After completing the tests, run:
cd C:\Projects\student-activity-platform\frontend npm run build Verify successful compilation and creation of the dist directory.
The Frontend is ready for further exercises involving activity management, data imports, attendance, and reconciliation.
Frontend deployment using AWS Amplify Hosting will be covered in the Application Deployment section.
Conclusion In this section, we tested the interface and main functionality groups of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
The React/Vite Frontend communicates with FastAPI through REST APIs, manages authentication sessions, and displays features appropriate for ADMIN and STUDENT users.
User-oriented testing helps identify interface, connectivity, authentication, and data issues before deploying the application on AWS.
In the next section, we will explore the detailed registration import and real-time Check-in/Check-out workflows.
Next: Registration and Attendance Management

title: Verify Analytics and Reports
content:
Verify Analytics and Reports In this section, we will verify the Analytics Dashboard and report Export functionality of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
The objective is to ensure that analytical indicators accurately reflect business records, exported reports contain the correct data scope, and users only access authorized information.
1. Prepare the testing environment Complete:
Section 5.6 - Registration and Attendance Management. Section 5.7 - Evidence Processing and Reconciliation. Section 5.8.1 - Prepare Analytics Data and Metrics. Section 5.8.2 - Build the Analytics Dashboard. Section 5.8.3 - Export CSV/XLSX Reports. Ensure that the following are available:
FastAPI Backend. React/Vite Frontend. ADMIN and STUDENT Demo accounts. An activity with test datasets. Exported report files. 2. Understand the verification workflow Business Data | v FastAPI Backend | +-------------------+ | | v v Analytics API Export Processing | | v v React Dashboard CSV / XLSX | | +---------+---------+ | v Data Verification Testing should verify that:
The Backend uses the correct source records. Metrics are aggregated within the correct scope. The Frontend displays accurate results. Reports do not contain unintended missing or duplicate records. Access permissions are enforced. 3. Define the test dataset Reuse the four-student Demo activity from section 5.7.
Source data:
Student ID Registration Check-in Check-out Evidence 0818000001 Yes Yes Yes Yes 0818000002 Yes Yes No Yes 0818000003 Yes No No Yes 0818000004 Yes Yes Yes No Participation results:
Student ID Status 0818000001 CONFIRMED 0818000002 Not yet confirmed 0818000003 REJECTED 0818000004 Not yet confirmed These synthetic records provide expected results for Dashboard verification.
4. Verify Analytics indicators Sign in using an ADMIN account and open the Analytics Dashboard.
Select the Demo activity if an activity filter is available.
Compare supported indicators with the following expected results:
Metric Expected Result Total Registrations 4 Total Check-in 3 Total Check-out 2 Complete Attendance 2 Evidence Submitted 3 Confirmed Participants 1 Rejected Participants 1 Awaiting Decision 2 Check-in Rate 75% Attendance Completion Rate 50% Confirmed Participation Rate 25% The example rates use total registrations as the denominator.
The current Dashboard is not required to display every indicator listed above.
Only compare metrics that use matching business definitions and data scopes.
5. Verify the Analytics API Open Swagger UI:
http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
Authenticate using an ADMIN account. Locate the statistics API used by the Dashboard. Provide the Activity ID or appropriate parameters. Execute the request. Inspect the response. Compare the values with the Dashboard. If the API response is correct but the Dashboard is incorrect, review:
Frontend response field mapping. Selected activity scope. Stored interface state. Additional Frontend calculations. Data refresh behavior. If the API response is incorrect, review Backend aggregation logic and source data.
6. Test activity filtering If activity filtering is supported, prepare two Demo activities.
Example:
Activity A: AWS Workshop Demo Registrations: 4 Confirmed Participants: 1 Activity B: Cloud Computing Seminar Registrations: 6 Confirmed Participants: 4 Perform the following:
Select Activity A. Verify its indicators. Select Activity B. Verify the new indicators. Return to the overall scope if supported. Expected results:
No unintended data mixing between activities. Correct Dashboard scope. Appropriate API request parameters. Updated analytical indicators. Aggregating both activities produces 10 registration records and 5 confirmed participation records.
This does not necessarily represent 10 unique students because individuals may register for multiple activities.
7. Test Participation updates Select a Demo record that has not received a final decision.
Open Participation. Review the student’s source records. Confirm or reject participation according to business requirements. Return to the Analytics Dashboard. Refresh data using the application’s supported mechanism. Inspect the updated indicators. If one eligible student changes to CONFIRMED:
Before: Confirmed Participants: 1 Awaiting Decision: 2 After: Confirmed Participants: 2 Awaiting Decision: 1 Updated rate:
Confirmed Participation Rate = 2 / 4 x 100 = 50% This is an illustrative scenario that assumes the student satisfies the confirmation requirements.
Do not assume that the Dashboard supports live WebSocket updates. Verify the current data refresh mechanism.
8. Test an empty dataset Create a Demo activity without registration records.
Open its Analytics view if supported.
Expected results:
No data retrieval errors. Appropriate count values. No NaN or Infinity rate values. No division-by-zero errors. An appropriate empty-data message. When the denominator is zero, display 0% or a not-applicable value according to the selected metric definition.
9. Verify exported reports Export a report for the Demo activity.
Open the downloaded CSV or XLSX file.
Verify:
The file opens successfully. Activity ID matches the selected activity. Student identifiers remain accurate. Registration and Attendance information is correct. CONFIRMED and REJECTED results match Backend records. No unintended duplicate records appear. Record counts match the selected report type. Examples:
A complete registration report may contain four student records. A confirmed-only report may contain one record before additional confirmation. A new confirmed-only report may contain two records after another valid confirmation. Different report types do not necessarily contain the same number of records.
10. Verify CSV reports using Python Create a separate practice file:
verify_export_report.py Content:
import csv from collections import Counter file_path = input( "Enter CSV file path: " ).strip().strip('"') with open( file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="" ) as file: reader = csv.DictReader(file) required_columns = { "activity_id", "mssv", "participation_status" } actual_columns = set( reader.fieldnames or [] ) missing_columns = ( required_columns - actual_columns ) if missing_columns: raise ValueError( f"Missing columns: {missing_columns}" ) rows = list(reader) keys = [ ( row["activity_id"].strip(), row["mssv"].strip() ) for row in rows ] key_counts = Counter(keys) duplicate_keys = [ key for key, count in key_counts.items() if count > 1 ] status_counts = Counter( row["participation_status"].strip() for row in rows ) print("Total rows:", len(rows)) print("Unique activity/student keys:", len(key_counts)) print("Duplicate keys:", duplicate_keys) print("Confirmed:", status_counts["CONFIRMED"]) print("Rejected:", status_counts["REJECTED"]) print("Other or unconfirmed:", len(rows) - status_counts["CONFIRMED"] - status_counts["REJECTED"]) Run:
python verify_export_report.py Enter the path of the CSV file to inspect.
Example:
C:\Projects\student-activity-platform\participation-report.csv Using the illustrative four-student report before additional confirmation, the expected output is:
Total rows: 4 Unique activity/student keys: 4 Duplicate keys: [] Confirmed: 1 Rejected: 1 Other or unconfirmed: 2 This script illustrates CSV verification for a report containing one row per student and activity. Column names, encoding, and delimiter must match the actual exported file. Reports containing multiple evidence or attendance records per student may legitimately contain repeated keys and require different verification rules.
11. Verify Amazon DynamoDB source data If the relevant AWS Pilots are enabled, verify source business records in DynamoDB.
Open:
Amazon DynamoDB Console
Select:
Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Inspect the following tables:
SAP-Activities. SAP-Registrations. SAP-Attendance. SAP-Evidence. SAP-Participation. Retrieve records by Activity ID using the procedures described in section 5.4.
Compare Registration, Attendance, and Participation records with the corresponding business results.
The Dashboard retrieves information through FastAPI rather than connecting directly to DynamoDB. DynamoDB verification confirms Cloud data storage within the relevant AWS Pilot scope. It does not establish that every Analytics API currently reads directly from DynamoDB.
12. Verify access permissions Use the two Demo accounts.
ADMIN Access administrative analytics. View authorized activity statistics. Export authorized administrative reports. STUDENT View personal participation information. Cannot access unauthorized administrative analytics. Cannot export other students’ information without permission. Test both the interface and REST APIs.
Protected APIs must reject authenticated users who lack the required permissions.
13. Troubleshoot common issues Issue What to Check Dashboard cannot load Backend, API URL, Access Token, and CORS Incorrect statistics Activity ID, scope, and aggregation logic Invalid rate Zero denominator or invalid source data Statistics not updated Data refresh mechanism Report download fails Export API or download handling Missing leading zeros CSV/XLSX data type handling Incorrect text encoding CSV encoding Incorrect activity in report Export parameters and filtering rules Missing DynamoDB records AWS Pilot and repository configuration 14. Summarize test results Test Case Expected Result Analytics API Correct data scope returned Dashboard Metrics Values match Backend results Participation Update Indicators update after data refresh Activity Filter Correct activity displayed when supported Empty Dataset No calculation errors CSV/XLSX Export Valid and readable file Report Data Records match the selected report type Student ID Formatting Identifiers preserved ADMIN Authorization Authorized administrative access STUDENT Authorization Unauthorized data access denied DynamoDB Verification Source records verified when Pilot is enabled Workshop participants should record actual results, capture supporting screenshots, and identify incomplete tests.
Conclusion In this section, we verified Analytics Dashboard and Export functionality in the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
By comparing Registration, Attendance, Evidence, and Participation records, the system can provide analytical indicators supporting student activity management.
The Dashboard uses React/Vite for visualization, while FastAPI handles business data processing and aggregation.
Exported reports help organizers access and review participation results consistently.
In the next section, we will deploy the Frontend using AWS Amplify Hosting and connect it to the FastAPI Backend through Cloudflare Quick Tunnel to create an Internet-accessible Demo environment.
Next: AWS Amplify and Cloudflare Tunnel Deployment

title: Verify Attendance Data
content:
Verify Attendance Data In this section, we will inspect and verify Check-in and Check-out records in the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
The objective is to ensure attendance records are associated with the correct student, activity, and timestamps, and can be used for post-event reconciliation.
1. Inspect the attendance list Sign in using an ADMIN account.
Open the Web Application. Select the Demo activity. Open the attendance list. Inspect the recorded Check-in and Check-out information. Review the following information:
Activity ID. Student ID. Student information. Check-in timestamp. Check-out timestamp. Attendance status. The records should match the operations performed in section 5.6.3.
2. Compare attendance with registration data Registration and Attendance represent different data groups.
Registration indicates that a student registered for an activity.
Attendance indicates whether a student has recorded Check-in and Check-out.
Example:
Student ID Registration Check-in Check-out 0818000001 Yes Yes Yes 0818000002 Yes Yes No 0818000003 Yes No No 0818000004 Yes Yes Yes From this illustrative dataset:
4 students registered. 3 students checked in. 2 students checked out. 1 student checked in but has no Check-out record. 1 student has no attendance record. These figures demonstrate the comparison process and do not represent actual test results.
3. Classify attendance scenarios Complete Check-in and Check-out records The student has both attendance timestamps.
These records provide input for additional participation verification.
Missing Check-out The student has checked in but does not have a Check-out record.
Organizers may need to investigate before confirming participation.
Missing attendance records The student may appear in the registration list but has not checked in.
Registration alone does not prove that the student attended the activity.
Inconsistent records Examples include:
A Check-out record without Check-in. A Check-out timestamp earlier than Check-in. Attendance associated with the wrong Activity ID. Student IDs inconsistent with student information. These cases should be investigated according to the Backend’s business rules and validation mechanisms.
4. Inspect attendance data through REST APIs Open Swagger UI:
http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
Locate the Attendance API group or activity-related data retrieval Endpoints.
Provide an ADMIN Access Token. Enter the Activity ID. Execute the request. Inspect the HTTP Status Code. Compare the Response Body with the Frontend attendance list. Use the attendance retrieval Endpoint defined in the current Backend Swagger UI.
Do not introduce a new Endpoint only for testing if the application already provides the required functionality.
5. Verify SQLite Local Persistence The project’s Demo version uses SQLite to support application state persistence and recovery.
To verify attendance persistence:
Record Check-in or Check-out for a Demo student. Record the Activity ID, Student ID, and timestamp. Inspect the data through the interface or REST API. Stop the Backend using Ctrl + C. Restart the Backend with the same Demo configuration. Inspect the previously recorded attendance information. Restart the Backend:
cd C:\Projects\student-activity-platform\backend .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 $env:SAP_DEMO_MODE="1" python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload The expected result is that records covered by the persistence mechanism remain recoverable after the Backend restarts.
If the records are missing, inspect the persistence module, configured data source, and Demo settings.
Do not delete the SQLite file or change its storage path during this test.
6. Verify data in Amazon DynamoDB If the Attendance AWS Pilot is enabled, attendance data can be inspected directly on AWS.
Open:
Amazon DynamoDB Console
Step 1: Select the AWS Region Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Step 2: Select the Attendance table In the DynamoDB Console:
Choose Tables. Select SAP-Attendance. Verify that the table status is ACTIVE. Step 3: Query records by Activity ID Choose Explore table items.
Select Query. Enter the Demo activity’s activity_id. Execute the query. Step 4: Inspect the item Select the record corresponding to a student whose attendance was recorded.
Inspect the actual attributes:
activity_id. mssv. Check-in timestamp. Check-out timestamp. Attendance attributes stored by the repository. Compare these values with the Backend response and Frontend display.
Verify DynamoDB records only when the corresponding Attendance AWS integration is enabled. A successful Check-in or Check-out API response does not automatically prove that data was written to DynamoDB.
7. Verify DynamoDB records using Python Use boto3 to retrieve an Attendance Record by Activity ID and Student ID.
Create a separate test file in the backend directory:
test_attendance_record.py Content:
import boto3 from pprint import pprint session = boto3.Session( profile_name="sap-dev", region_name="ap-southeast-1" ) dynamodb = session.resource("dynamodb") table = dynamodb.Table("SAP-Attendance") activity_id = input("Activity ID: ").strip() mssv = input("Student ID: ").strip() response = table.get_item( Key={ "activity_id": activity_id, "mssv": mssv }, ConsistentRead=True ) item = response.get("Item") if item: print("Attendance record found") pprint(item) else: print("Attendance record not found") Run:
python test_attendance_record.py Enter the Activity ID and Student ID of the test record.
The script uses the sap-dev AWS Profile and requires dynamodb:GetItem permission for SAP-Attendance.
The key structure must match the table verified in section 5.4.
The script is read-only and does not update or delete DynamoDB items.
8. Verify data access permissions Test the ADMIN and STUDENT roles.
ADMIN View attendance lists for authorized activities. Inspect student attendance information within administrative permissions. Perform authorized attendance management operations. STUDENT View personal participation information within the authorized scope. Cannot access unauthorized administrative attendance lists. Cannot modify another student’s attendance records. Verify both the interface and REST APIs to ensure Backend authorization is enforced.
9. Verify data consistency Compare the following data sources:
Component Verification Registration Student and activity association Frontend Displayed attendance status Backend Data returned through REST APIs SQLite Records covered by Local Persistence DynamoDB Cloud records when AWS Pilot is enabled If discrepancies are identified:
Verify the Activity ID. Verify the Student ID. Inspect interface filters. Check timestamps and time zones. Review repository and AWS Pilot settings. Inspect Backend read/write errors. Matching local and DynamoDB records in a test does not demonstrate that the entire system supports automatic bidirectional synchronization.
10. Prepare data for reconciliation After verifying attendance records, we will use them as inputs for participation reconciliation.
Example:
Student ID: 0818000001 Registration: YES Check-in: Recorded Check-out: Recorded Evidence: Not yet verified Participation: Not yet confirmed Having both Check-in and Check-out records does not automatically mean that every participation requirement has been satisfied.
Some activities may require additional evidence or other conditions.
The next workflow is:
Registration Data + Attendance Data + Evidence Data | v Reconciliation | v ADMIN Confirmation | v Participation Result Final participation confirmation must follow the activity’s business rules and appropriate administrative decisions.
11. Summarize test results Test Expected Result Registration List Correct registered students displayed Check-in Correct student and activity recorded Check-out Correct Attendance Record updated Duplicate Operation No duplicate attendance record Time Validation Attendance time rules enforced Backend Authorization Unauthorized access denied Local Persistence Covered records recoverable DynamoDB Verification Item available when AWS Pilot is enabled Data Consistency Records match performed operations Workshop participants should record actual results and capture corresponding screenshots for each test.
Conclusion In this section, we completed the registration and attendance management workflow of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
Registration data is imported from the University Portal, while Attendance data is recorded directly in real time through FastAPI REST APIs.
By comparing Frontend, Backend, SQLite, and Amazon DynamoDB records, we gained a better understanding of data accuracy and persistence verification in a practical management system.
In the next section, we will import participation evidence from Google Forms/Google Sheets, reconcile data, and confirm student participation results.
Next: Evidence Processing and Reconciliation

title: Verify Clean-up and Review Workshop
content:
Verify Clean-up and Review Workshop In this final section, we will verify resource management results and review the skills applied throughout the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform Workshop.
The objective is to confirm that the Demo environment has been stopped appropriately, important resources remain protected, and workshop evidence has been documented.
1. Verify the local environment Open PowerShell and inspect port 8001:
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8001 -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Verify:
FastAPI Demo is stopped if no longer needed. Cloudflare Quick Tunnel is stopped. Vite Development Server is stopped when unused. Source code remains available. Required SQLite Demo data is preserved. If the Backend is needed for another demonstration, document its active state rather than requiring shutdown.
2. Verify AWS Amplify Open AWS Amplify Console.
Verify:
The Amplify App remains available if required. The main branch is still deployed. Build History can be accessed. The Website URL has been documented. The Backend connection uses a temporary Tunnel URL. If the Tunnel is stopped, Frontend assets may still load while Backend-dependent features remain unavailable.
This matches the current Demo architecture.
3. Verify Amazon DynamoDB Open DynamoDB Console in ap-southeast-1.
Retain the following tables if still needed:
SAP-Activities SAP-Registrations SAP-Attendance SAP-Evidence SAP-Participation Inspect table status and required backups.
Demo data does not need to be deleted if it remains necessary for internship reporting.
4. Verify Amazon S3 Open S3 Console and select:
sap-data-project-2026-huflit01 Review data requiring retention.
If Lambda demonstrations will continue, preserve:
lambda-demo/input/registrations.csv lambda-demo/processed/registrations-result.json Confirm that no important Objects have been accidentally deleted.
5. Verify AWS Lambda and IAM If the following Function is retained:
sap-csv-processor-demo Verify:
The Function exists. The Execution Role is correctly configured. Required IAM Policies remain attached. No unintended changes have been made. The Test Event can be reused when needed. Another Lambda invocation is not required merely to confirm that the resource exists and its configuration is intact.
6. Verify Amazon CloudWatch Inspect:
/aws/lambda/sap-csv-processor-demo If retained:
Verify Log Retention. Review required execution evidence. Save screenshots before important Logs expire. The exercise used a seven-day retention period. Older Logs may no longer be available during later reviews.
7. Review final Billing information Open AWS Billing and Cost Management.
Inspect:
Service-level costs. Remaining resources. The selected reporting period. Any charges requiring continued monitoring. Do not assume that stopping local services eliminates all AWS charges.
8. Review the AWS services used The project and Workshop explored six main AWS services.
Service Project Role AWS Amplify Hosting React/Vite Frontend deployment Amazon DynamoDB Cloud business data storage testing Amazon S3 CSV and JSON storage AWS Lambda Serverless CSV processing AWS IAM Resource access management Amazon CloudWatch Lambda logging and monitoring Supporting technologies:
FastAPI Backend. React/Vite Frontend. SQLite Local Persistence. Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. GitHub. Python and boto3. 9. Review implemented functionality The Workshop covered:
Student activity management. ADMIN/STUDENT authentication and authorization. CSV/XLSX registration imports. Real-time Check-in and Check-out. Evidence imports from Google Forms/Google Sheets. Registration, Attendance, and Evidence reconciliation. Participation confirmation. Analytics Dashboard. Report Export. Frontend deployment and Demo Backend connectivity. Serverless CSV processing using Lambda and S3. These features were developed and tested at different scopes. The system should not be described as fully migrated to AWS Production.
10. Summarize verified results Area Recorded Scope Frontend Deployment Amplify Hosting Backend Connectivity Cloudflare Quick Tunnel ADMIN/STUDENT Login Tested Activity Creation Tested in Demo DynamoDB Integration AWS Pilot S3 CSV Processing Lambda Test Event CSV Result 4 records: 2 valid, 1 duplicate, 1 invalid Output Storage S3 JSON Object Monitoring CloudWatch Logs These results represent the previously recorded testing scope.
Comprehensive Load Testing, Production Backend deployment, and high-concurrency verification have not been established.
11. Review learning outcomes Throughout the Workshop, learners practiced:
Designing Cloud-connected Web architectures. Developing REST APIs using Python/FastAPI. Building React/Vite interfaces. Organizing and processing student activity data. Integrating Amazon DynamoDB. Deploying Frontend applications using AWS Amplify Hosting. Building AWS Lambda processing functions. Managing access with IAM. Monitoring execution using CloudWatch. Reviewing costs and managing AWS resource lifecycles. These are foundational skills for Cloud Computing and Data Engineering.
12. Explore future improvements Potential improvements include:
Hosting FastAPI on a Cloud service with a stable Endpoint. Extending DynamoDB integration where appropriate. Automating S3 and Lambda processing. Improving monitoring and alerting. Strengthening security and Secret management. Performing performance and concurrent load testing. Improving deployment automation. Developing operational and data recovery documentation. These items are future improvements rather than completed components of the existing Demo.
13. Complete the workshop checklist Item Status to Verify Source code preserved Check Workshop documentation completed Check Evidence screenshots prepared Check Demo environment stopped appropriately Check AWS resources inventoried Check Required data preserved Check AWS costs reviewed Check Test resources managed Check Update each item based on the actual environment.
Conclusion The Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform Workshop provided practical experience across Web Application development and AWS integration.
Through Amplify Hosting, DynamoDB, S3, Lambda, IAM, and CloudWatch, learners explored application deployment, data storage, processing, and monitoring in a Cloud environment.
Combining Registration, Attendance, Evidence, Reconciliation, and Participation demonstrated how a data-driven platform can support a real-world educational management problem.
Resource lifecycle management at the end of the Workshop helps ensure that the exercise concludes safely, unnecessary costs are limited, and important project data remains available.
Workshop Completed – Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.

title: Verify data in the AWS Console
content:
Verify Data in the AWS Console In this section, we will use the AWS Management Console to inspect data stored in the Amazon DynamoDB tables of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
The objective is to compare data across the FastAPI Backend, local SQLite environment, and Amazon DynamoDB.
1. Open the Amazon DynamoDB Console Open the Amazon DynamoDB Console.
Select the AWS Region:
Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 In the navigation pane, choose Tables.
Verify the five project tables.
Ensure that the tables have an ACTIVE status.
2. Verify Activities data Select SAP-Activities.
Choose Explore table items.
Switch to Query mode when searching by Partition Key.
Enter the Activity ID created in section 5.4.3 into the activity_id field.
Run the query.
During an earlier AWS integration test, the project used the following Activity ID:
ACT#AWSTEST-9198ABC48900 This identifier represents a historical integration test record. For a new workshop execution, use the Activity ID returned by the API in the previous section.
Inspect:
Activity ID. Activity name. Location. Scheduled time. Activity status. Compare these values with the Backend Response.
Matching data confirms that the Activity has been stored in DynamoDB.
3. Verify Registrations data Return to the Tables list.
Select SAP-Registrations.
Choose Explore table items.
Select Query.
Enter the activity_id of the activity to inspect.
Execute the query.
Inspect the following:
activity_id. mssv. Registration information. Business attributes stored by the current repository implementation. Compare the number of registrations with the data imported from CSV/XLSX files.
Each student’s registration within an activity is identified by the combination of activity_id and mssv.
4. Verify Attendance data Select SAP-Attendance.
Choose Explore table items.
Query records using activity_id.
Select the test student’s item.
Inspect Check-in and Check-out data recorded through the API.
Verify:
The Student ID matches the student who recorded attendance. The Activity ID matches the selected activity. Check-in and Check-out timestamps are appropriate. Attendance information is consistent with the Backend. Pay attention to time zone representation. The application’s attendance business logic uses Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, while stored timestamps may use a different time representation.
Attendance is recorded in real time. Separate Check-in and Check-out files do not need to be imported after the activity.
5. Verify Evidence data Select SAP-Evidence.
Choose Explore table items.
Query records using activity_id.
Inspect items with mssv as the Sort Key.
Compare the records with the evidence file imported through the Backend.
During the project’s AWS Pilot test on November 6, 2026, three synthetic Evidence records were verified in DynamoDB.
This result illustrates how Evidence data can be stored using Activity ID and Student ID.
When performing the workshop, the number of records should reflect the actual input dataset.
6. Verify Participation data Select SAP-Participation.
Choose Explore table items.
Select Query.
Enter the activity_id of the activity that has completed reconciliation.
Inspect the returned items.
Relevant business attributes include:
activity_id. mssv. Attendance status. Evidence status. Reconciliation result. Participation confirmation status. During an earlier AWS Pilot test, three synthetic records were retrieved from SAP-Participation.
Some records contained information such as:
NO_ATTENDANCE REJECTED evidence_status: YES This illustrates that a student may submit participation evidence but still have missing attendance information, resulting in an unconfirmed participation outcome according to business rules or ADMIN decisions.
Submitting evidence alone does not automatically guarantee confirmed participation.
7. Verify data using AWS CLI In addition to the AWS Console, AWS CLI can retrieve an Activity from SAP-Activities.
Run:
aws dynamodb get-item ` --table-name SAP-Activities ` --key '{"activity_id":{"S":"ACT#AWSTEST-9198ABC48900"}}' ` --consistent-read ` --region ap-southeast-1 ` --profile sap-dev Replace the Activity ID with the actual identifier to inspect.
If the item exists, the Response contains the Item field and its attributes.
To query Evidence records for an activity:
aws dynamodb query ` --table-name SAP-Evidence ` --key-condition-expression "activity_id = :aid" ` --expression-attribute-values '{":aid":{"S":"ACT#AWSTEST-9198ABC48900"}}' ` --consistent-read ` --region ap-southeast-1 ` --profile sap-dev You can replace SAP-Evidence with SAP-Registrations, SAP-Attendance, or SAP-Participation to inspect other business data groups.

8. Compare SQLite and DynamoDB data In the Demo version, SQLite continues to support local application persistence and recovery.
To verify data consistency:
Select a Demo activity. Identify its Activity ID. Inspect its data through the REST APIs. Inspect local data covered by SQLite persistence. Query the corresponding DynamoDB records. Compare record counts and relevant business attributes. Verification table:
Data Backend/SQLite DynamoDB Activities Verify Activity ID and status SAP-Activities Registrations Verify registration records SAP-Registrations Attendance Verify Check-in/Check-out data SAP-Attendance Evidence Verify participation evidence SAP-Evidence Participation Verify confirmation results SAP-Participation During previous project tests, Evidence and Participation data were compared with corresponding local records.

9. Troubleshoot common issues Error Possible Cause ResourceNotFoundException Incorrect Region or table name AccessDeniedException Missing IAM permissions ValidationException Incorrect Key Schema or data types Item not found Incorrect Activity ID or data has not been written to DynamoDB Successful API but empty DynamoDB table The API may use SQLite or its AWS Pilot is not enabled Mismatched record counts Check input data, filters, and processing behavior 10. Completion results After completing this section, we have:
Verified the status of five DynamoDB tables. Inspected Activities data. Inspected Registrations data. Inspected Attendance data. Inspected Evidence data. Inspected Participation data. Used AWS Console and AWS CLI to retrieve records. Compared Cloud data with Backend business data. Conclusion Amazon DynamoDB allows the project to explore NoSQL data storage on AWS.
Through this section, we learned how to design tables, configure boto3, integrate the Backend, test data reading and writing, and verify results using the AWS Management Console.
DynamoDB integration represents an important step in extending the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform from a local development environment toward a Cloud architecture.
SQLite remains part of the current Demo, while DynamoDB supports the Cloud storage workflows that have been integrated and tested.
In the next section, we will develop and configure the React/Vite Frontend to communicate with the FastAPI Backend.

title: Verify Participation Results
content:
Verify Participation Results In this section, we will verify reconciliation and participation confirmation results in the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform.
The objective is to ensure that Participation records are associated with the correct student, activity, and confirmation status, and can be used for Analytics Dashboard and Export.
1. Inspect the Participation list Sign in using an ADMIN account.
Open the Web Application. Select the Demo activity. Open Participation Management. Review reconciled student records. Inspect the confirmation statuses. Review the following information:
Activity ID. Student ID. Registration. Check-in. Check-out. Evidence. Reconciliation Result. Participation Status. The results must match the operations performed in section 5.7.3.
2. Compare source data and confirmation results Use the synthetic dataset from previous exercises:
Student ID Registration Check-in Check-out Evidence 0818000001 Yes Yes Yes Yes 0818000002 Yes Yes No Yes 0818000003 Yes No No Yes 0818000004 Yes Yes Yes No Illustrative outcomes after the two ADMIN decisions in section 5.7.3:
Student ID Confirmation Result 0818000001 CONFIRMED 0818000002 Not yet confirmed 0818000003 REJECTED 0818000004 Not yet confirmed “Not yet confirmed” is a business description rather than a newly introduced Backend status.
This example contains:
Total registrations: 4. Confirmed participants: 1. Rejected participants: 1. Students awaiting a final decision: 2. These are synthetic workshop figures, not actual university activity results.
3. Verify results through REST APIs Open Swagger UI:
http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
Locate the Participation retrieval Endpoint defined in the current Backend.
Perform the following:
Provide an ADMIN Access Token. Enter the Activity ID. Execute the request. Inspect the HTTP Status Code. Inspect records in the Response. Compare the results with the Frontend. Do not create a new Endpoint if the Backend already provides the necessary retrieval functionality.
4. Verify SQLite Local Persistence The Demo version uses SQLite to support local persistence and application state recovery.
To verify participation persistence:
Confirm or reject a Demo student. Record the Activity ID, Student ID, and status. Verify the result through the REST API. Stop FastAPI using Ctrl + C. Restart the Backend with the same configuration. Retrieve the Participation Record again. Restart the Backend:
cd C:\Projects\student-activity-platform\backend .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 $env:SAP_DEMO_MODE="1" python -m uvicorn app.main:app --reload The expected result is that records covered by the persistence mechanism remain recoverable after restarting the Backend.
If records are missing, review:
SAP_DEMO_MODE configuration. SQLite storage location. Persistence module. Repository and configured data source. Backend startup logs. Do not delete the SQLite file during verification.
5. Verify Evidence in Amazon DynamoDB If the Evidence AWS Pilot is enabled:
Open the Amazon DynamoDB Console. Select Singapore - ap-southeast-1. Select SAP-Evidence. Verify the ACTIVE status. Choose Explore table items. Select Query. Enter the target activity_id. Execute the query. Inspect the items associated with the Demo students.
During the project’s AWS Pilot test on November 6, 2026, three synthetic Evidence records were verified in DynamoDB.
Actual workshop record counts depend on the imported dataset.
6. Verify Participation in Amazon DynamoDB If the Participation AWS Pilot is enabled:
Return to the Tables list. Select SAP-Participation. Choose Explore table items. Select Query. Enter the Activity ID of the reconciled activity. Execute the query. Inspect the actual item attributes:
activity_id. mssv. Attendance status. Evidence status. Reconciliation result. Participation confirmation status. Exact attribute names must match the stored item and current repository implementation.
During a previous AWS integration test, three synthetic Participation records were retrieved.
Some records contained:
NO_ATTENDANCE REJECTED evidence_status: YES This illustrates a scenario where a student has evidence but lacks attendance records and is not confirmed for participation.
Three records represent an earlier project test result, not a required workshop record count. New workshop data must be verified using the actual Activity ID and Student ID.
7. Verify records using boto3 Python can retrieve Evidence and Participation records for the same activity.
Create a separate test script:
backend/test_participation_verification.py Content:
import boto3 from boto3.dynamodb.conditions import Key session = boto3.Session( profile_name="sap-dev", region_name="ap-southeast-1" ) dynamodb = session.resource("dynamodb") activity_id = input("Activity ID: ").strip() if not activity_id: raise ValueError("Activity ID is required") tables = [ "SAP-Evidence", "SAP-Participation" ] for table_name in tables: table = dynamodb.Table(table_name) records = [] params = { "KeyConditionExpression": Key("activity_id").eq(activity_id), "ConsistentRead": True } while True: response = table.query(**params) records.extend( response.get("Items", []) ) last_key = response.get("LastEvaluatedKey") if not last_key: break params["ExclusiveStartKey"] = last_key print("\nTable:", table_name) print("Total records:", len(records)) for record in records: print("Student ID:", record.get("mssv")) Run:
cd C:\Projects\student-activity-platform\backend .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 python test_participation_verification.py Enter the Activity ID to inspect.
The script uses the sap-dev AWS Profile and requires dynamodb:Query permissions for the relevant tables.
It handles pagination using LastEvaluatedKey to retrieve all result pages for the selected activity.
The script only reads records and displays Student IDs. It does not update or delete data.
8. Inspect an individual student record Use GetItem to verify a specific student’s Participation Record.
Example:
import boto3 from pprint import pprint session = boto3.Session( profile_name="sap-dev", region_name="ap-southeast-1" ) dynamodb = session.resource("dynamodb") table = dynamodb.Table("SAP-Participation") activity_id = input("Activity ID: ").strip() mssv = input("Student ID: ").strip() response = table.get_item( Key={ "activity_id": activity_id, "mssv": mssv }, ConsistentRead=True ) item = response.get("Item") if item: print("Participation record found") pprint(item) else: print("Participation record not found") This example requires dynamodb:GetItem permission.
The key structure must match the SAP-Participation Key Schema verified in section 5.4.
If no item is returned, verify Activity ID, Student ID, AWS Profile, Region, and AWS Pilot configuration.
A missing DynamoDB item does not automatically demonstrate a failed confirmation when the Backend uses local persistence.
9. Verify the STUDENT interface Sign out of the ADMIN account.
Sign in using the Demo STUDENT account associated with a confirmed participation record.
Verify:
The student can view authorized personal participation information. The correct activity is displayed. The confirmation status matches the Backend. Administrative confirmation controls are unavailable. Other students’ information cannot be accessed without authorization. Repeat the test with a rejected Demo record if a corresponding test account is available.
If the current interface does not display a particular status, record the actual behavior for future Frontend improvements.
10. Verify data consistency Compare the following components:
Component Verification Registration Student registration information Attendance Check-in and Check-out records Evidence Participation evidence Reconciliation Consolidated evaluation results Participation Final confirmation results Frontend Role-appropriate displayed information SQLite Records covered by local persistence DynamoDB Cloud records when AWS Pilot is enabled If discrepancies are identified:
Verify Activity ID. Verify Student ID. Review the latest source data. Verify whether reconciliation results are current. Inspect repository configuration. Review Backend logs. Inspect AWS storage results. Matching local and DynamoDB records in one test does not prove complete migration or automatic bidirectional synchronization.
11. Prepare data for Analytics Dashboard After verification, Participation becomes an important source for analytical indicators.
Example:
Total Registrations: 4 Confirmed Participants: 1 Rejected Participants: 1 Unconfirmed Students: 2 The confirmed participation rate among registered students is:
Participation Rate = Confirmed Registered Students / Total Registrations x 100 = 1 / 4 x 100 = 25% This illustrative result represents a point in time before all administrative decisions are finalized.
The rate may change after additional participation decisions.
Analytical metrics should use consistent business definitions and distinguish between:
Registered students. Students with Check-in records. Students with complete attendance records. Confirmed participants. Analytics and Export functionality will be covered in section 5.8.
12. Summarize test results Test Expected Result Evidence Import Evidence data processed Reconciliation Three source datasets matched correctly CONFIRMED Correct confirmation result stored REJECTED Correct rejection result stored ADMIN Authorization Administrative operations permitted STUDENT Authorization Only authorized information accessible Local Persistence Covered records recoverable SAP-Evidence Records accessible when AWS Pilot is enabled SAP-Participation Results accessible when AWS Pilot is enabled Data Consistency Results match business records Workshop participants should record actual results and capture corresponding screenshots.
Do not disclose real student information or AWS authentication credentials in DynamoDB Console, Terminal, or REST API screenshots.
Conclusion In this section, we completed the evidence processing, reconciliation, and student participation confirmation workflow.
Data from the University Portal, Attendance records, and Google Forms/Google Sheets was combined to support ADMIN business decisions.
Through FastAPI REST APIs, SQLite Local Persistence, and Amazon DynamoDB integration, we can verify the application’s data processing and storage behavior.
Participation results provide a foundation for Analytics Dashboard, student engagement analysis, and report exports.
Next: Analytics Dashboard and Export

title: Verify the Deployed Application
content:
Verify the Deployed Application In this section, we will verify the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform after deploying its Frontend using AWS Amplify Hosting and connecting the Backend through Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
The objective is to validate the complete workflow from the browser to the Frontend, FastAPI Backend, and configured data persistence in the Demo environment.
1. Prepare the testing environment Ensure that the following components are available:
Deployed AWS Amplify Frontend. Successful main branch deployment. FastAPI Demo Backend on port 8001. Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. SQLite Demo Persistence. ADMIN and STUDENT Demo accounts. The previous deployment used:
Frontend: https://main.d2p96elhe5x6se.amplifyapp.com Backend HTTPS: https://replies-cabinet-recipes-prevent.trycloudflare.com Backend Local: http://127.0.0.1:8001 Use the actual active Amplify and Tunnel addresses during a new workshop execution.
The Cloudflare URL above is a historical testing address. Do not assume that it remains accessible after the Quick Tunnel process has stopped.
2. Review the deployment architecture Browser | +---- HTTPS ----> AWS Amplify Hosting | React / Vite | +---- HTTPS ----> Cloudflare Quick Tunnel | v FastAPI Backend 127.0.0.1:8001 | v SQLite Demo Data The browser loads the Frontend from AWS Amplify and sends API requests to Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
FastAPI receives requests, validates authentication, processes business operations, and stores data according to its Demo configuration.
When AWS Pilot integration is enabled, applicable business workflows may also interact with Amazon DynamoDB.
3. Verify Backend Health Open PowerShell:
Invoke-RestMethod ` -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:8001/health" Verify the HTTPS Endpoint:
$tunnelUrl = "https://YOUR-TUNNEL.trycloudflare.com" Invoke-RestMethod ` -Uri "$tunnelUrl/health" Replace YOUR-TUNNEL with the actual Tunnel hostname.
Expected results:
The local Backend responds successfully. The Cloudflare HTTPS Endpoint responds successfully. Requests are forwarded to the correct Backend on port 8001. During the November 9, 2026 test, the HTTPS Health Endpoint was verified successfully.
4. Verify the AWS Amplify interface Open the deployed Amplify Website.
Verify that:
The Website uses HTTPS. The login page is displayed. CSS and JavaScript assets work correctly. No critical resource loading errors occur. Displaying the login page only confirms Frontend Hosting availability. Authentication testing is necessary to verify Backend connectivity.
5. Inspect API requests from the Website Press F12 to open Developer Tools.
Select Network. Select Fetch/XHR. Perform a login operation. Open the POST /auth/login request. Inspect the Request URL. Expected URL:
POST https://YOUR-TUNNEL.trycloudflare.com/auth/login The request must not target localhost on the user’s device.
Also inspect:
HTTP Method. HTTP Status Code. Response Body. Request Origin. CORS Response Headers. During the previous deployment test, login requests from the Amplify Website were confirmed to reach the Cloudflare HTTPS Endpoint.
6. Test invalid login credentials Use a Demo account with an incorrect password.
Attempt to sign in through the Amplify Website.
Expected result:
HTTP 401 Unauthorized The interface should display an appropriate login failure message.
During the November 9, 2026 test, invalid credentials produced an HTTP 401 response.
This confirms that the request reached the Backend and authentication validation was performed.
HTTP 401 is the expected result of this negative test, not a Cloudflare Tunnel failure.
7. Test ADMIN login Return to the login page. Enter valid ADMIN Demo credentials. Sign in. Inspect the administrative Home page. Verify ADMIN functionality. Expected results:
Successful login. Valid authentication information returned by the Backend. Updated Frontend authentication session. Appropriate administrative functionality displayed. Inspect /auth/me if the Frontend uses this Endpoint to retrieve current user information.
ADMIN login through the deployed Amplify Website passed during the previous project test.
8. Test activity creation From the ADMIN interface:
Open Activity Management. Select the new activity function. Enter Demo activity information. Save the activity. Illustrative information:
Activity Name: Amplify Deployment Demo Location: University Hall Description: Testing Frontend and Backend integration after AWS deployment. Complete the required date, time, and other fields using the actual application form.
Expected results:
The Frontend submits a request through Cloudflare Tunnel. The Backend processes activity creation. An Activity ID is generated. The activity appears in the list. Record the actual Activity ID for subsequent verification.
During the November 9, 2026 deployment test, creating and saving an activity through the Amplify Website passed.
9. Verify data after refreshing After creating an activity:
Record its name and Activity ID. Press F5 to reload the page. Open the activity list again. Inspect the newly created activity. Expected results:
The activity remains retrievable from the Backend. Reloading the Frontend does not remove the stored activity. Displayed information matches the API response. For SQLite Persistence verification, additionally restart the Backend with the same Demo configuration according to section 5.3.2.
A successful browser refresh alone does not prove data recovery after a Backend restart.
10. Test STUDENT login Sign out of the ADMIN account.
Sign in using a STUDENT Demo account.
Verify:
The student Home page is displayed. Authorized personal functionality is available. Student Account Management is not displayed. Unauthorized participation confirmation or activity management is restricted. Verify STUDENT access restrictions for administrative APIs.
Example:
GET /admin/students The Backend must deny access when the user lacks ADMIN permissions.
STUDENT login passed during the earlier deployment test.
11. Test additional business functionality After validating authentication and activity creation, test the business workflows available in the Demo.
Feature Test Registration Import Import CSV/XLSX registration records Check-in / Check-out Record student attendance in real time Evidence Import Import participation evidence Reconciliation Compare student records Participation Confirm or reject participation Analytics Dashboard Display analytical indicators Export Download supported report formats Use synthetic datasets and appropriate Demo activities.
These additional tests evaluate the complete business workflow in the deployed environment.
Do not assume every feature has passed solely because authentication and activity creation work.
12. Verify using another browser or device Open the Amplify Website using another browser or an authorized Demo device.
Use Demo credentials to verify login and application access.
The objective is to confirm that the Frontend does not depend on localhost on the user’s device.
The other device does not need Python or FastAPI because its browser communicates with the Cloudflare HTTPS Endpoint.
The Backend must remain running on the computer hosting cloudflared.
13. Test Backend or Tunnel interruption In a dedicated test environment:
Inspect the Website when the Backend is temporarily unavailable. Review Frontend connectivity error messages. Restart the Backend using the same configuration. Verify the Health Endpoint. Check whether connectivity is restored. If cloudflared is stopped and a new Quick Tunnel is created, update VITE_API_BASE_URL and redeploy the Frontend.
The Amplify Website may still display its interface while the Backend is unavailable.
This illustrates the difference between Frontend Hosting Availability and Backend API Availability.
14. Summarize deployment test results Results recorded during the November 9, 2026 deployment:
Test Result Amplify main deployment PASS FastAPI Demo port 8001 PASS Cloudflare HTTPS Health PASS VITE_API_BASE_URL configuration PASS Amplify Redeploy PASS Login Request through Tunnel PASS Invalid Login - HTTP 401 PASS ADMIN Login PASS STUDENT Login PASS Create and Save Activity PASS These results represent the verified deployment test scope.
Additional testing is required where evidence is not yet available:
Complete business workflows on the deployed Website. Concurrent user access. Performance and load capacity. Recovery from Backend interruptions. Production security readiness. 15. Evaluate the Demo architecture Advantages:
Frontend hosting on AWS Amplify. HTTPS Website access. Internet connectivity to a local Backend. Convenient application demonstrations and testing. Suitable for Cloud Computing learning. Limitations:
The Backend depends on a local computer. Quick Tunnel uses a temporary address. Frontend redeployment is required when the API URL changes. SQLite Demo Persistence has not been entirely replaced by a Cloud Database. A highly available and scalable Production Backend has not yet been established. Future improvements:
Deploy the Backend using an appropriate Cloud service. Establish a stable Backend Endpoint. Complete Cloud data storage integration. Strengthen security, monitoring, and credential management. Perform Load Testing and performance evaluation. These are proposed future improvements, not completed deployment components.
Conclusion In this section, we completed the deployment and verification of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform using AWS Amplify Hosting and Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
The React/Vite Frontend was deployed to a Cloud environment and communicates with the FastAPI Demo Backend through HTTPS REST APIs.
Successful ADMIN/STUDENT login, Health checks, API connectivity, and activity creation demonstrate integration between the deployed Frontend and local Backend.
In the next section, we will explore serverless CSV processing using Amazon S3 and AWS Lambda, with IAM permissions for resource access.
Next: Serverless Data Processing with Amazon S3 and AWS Lambda

title: Worklog Week 4
content:

title: Frontend Development with React/Vite
content:
Frontend Development with React/Vite In this section, we will develop and configure the Frontend of the Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform using React and Vite.
React is a JavaScript library used to build component-based user interfaces. Vite is a Frontend development and build tool that provides fast startup and automatic interface updates when source code changes.
The Frontend serves as the primary interaction layer between users and the system.
The main features include:
User login and authentication. ADMIN and STUDENT role-based interfaces. Student activity management. Student account management. Registration data imports from CSV/XLSX files. Real-time Check-in and Check-out recording. Participation evidence imports. Data reconciliation and participation confirmation. Analytics Dashboard and report exports. Personal profile management. Frontend Architecture ADMIN / STUDENT | v React / Vite Frontend | | REST API + Access Token v Python / FastAPI Backend | +-- SQLite Local Persistence | +-- Amazon DynamoDB Integration In the development environment, the Frontend runs locally and sends REST API requests to the FastAPI Backend on port 8000.
After development and testing, the Frontend will be deployed using AWS Amplify Hosting. Cloudflare Quick Tunnel provides connectivity between the deployed Frontend and the local Backend in the Demo environment.
Contents Set up and run the React/Vite Frontend Connect the Frontend to FastAPI REST APIs Implement ADMIN/STUDENT authentication and authorization Test the interface and system functionality Objectives After completing this section, you will be able to:
Understand the Frontend structure of a React/Vite Web Application. Install dependencies and run the application locally. Connect React to the FastAPI Backend through REST APIs. Understand Access Token and login session management. Develop interfaces appropriate for ADMIN and STUDENT users. Test the main system features. Prepare the Frontend for deployment using AWS Amplify Hosting. Through this section, learners will understand how user interfaces communicate with Backend services and data storage components in a complete Web Application.

title: Workshop
content:
Workshop – Student Activity Management & Engagement Analytics Platform This hands-on workshop documents the actual implementation and testing of a student activity management and engagement analytics platform. Its main application uses React/Vite, FastAPI and SQLite; AWS Amplify hosts the frontend; DynamoDB was tested for cloud data storage; and a separate Amazon S3 / AWS Lambda CSV-processing demo uses IAM and CloudWatch.
Workshop contents Introduction and architecture Prerequisites FastAPI backend development DynamoDB integration and testing React/Vite frontend development Registration and real-time attendance Evidence import, reconciliation and participation confirmation Analytics dashboard and report export Deployment and testing Serverless CSV processing with Amazon S3 and AWS Lambda AWS resource cleanup and verification Implementation boundary: FastAPI is a locally run demo backend, not an AWS-hosted production API. The Lambda pipeline was tested separately from the application’s normal CSV/XLSX import functionality.
